text: After this you can prepare a proposed online workshop for interruptions.

A multi-team event needs explicit roles, stage instructions, accessible controls and a fallback procedure. Instructions should tell each participant what to do and when a phase is complete. Facilitators need a shared plan for reconnecting, pausing and recovering agreed results. English and French support is a product target, not a verified capability of this guide.

items: Check room roles, team counts and expected session length. You should see: A feasible plan with clear responsibilities. If not: Adjust the event before participants join.
Provide a short instruction for each stage. You should see: A stated task, warning and completion condition. If not: Rewrite a step that requires unstated facilitator knowledge.
Test reconnect and recovery with a lost connection. You should see: A known route back to committed state. If not: Pause the room and use the approved fallback.
Close the session and retain only necessary records. You should see: A debrief and controlled export or disposal plan. If not: Reconcile outstanding actions before closure.
Inferred: A facilitator loses access during bidding. The event pauses until the authoritative state is recovered.

text: Plan for interruption before the workshop starts.
A manual fallback must not silently change the announced rules.

items: Assuming two languages are supported because buttons translate. Rules, feedback and facilitator instructions may remain untranslated. Fix: Review the full experience with qualified readers.
